_Triggers: 1 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; regulatory action: Florida Department of Financial Services; CEO changed during fiscal year._

Kemper Corp operates two primary insurance segments serving niche and underserved markets across the United States. The Specialty Property & Casualty Insurance segment, based in Chicago, conducts personal automobile insurance under the Kemper Auto brand in 22 states, along with commercial automobile coverage and specialty automobile products. The Life Insurance segment, headquartered in St. Louis, provides individual life and supplemental accident and health insurance through approximately 2,200 career agents across 26 states and the District of Columbia. Revenue grew 3.3% to $4.8 billion in the most recent fiscal year, with net income of $143.3 million. Kemper positions itself as a specialized insurer in niche markets, emphasizing pricing segmentation discipline, timely claims settlement, technological innovation in sales and marketing, and expense control to compete against larger property and casualty insurers and established life and health insurance groups.

Florida insurance reform enacted in 2023 has imposed material constraints on Kemper's underwriting profitability. The law introduced profit limit restrictions on personal auto underwriting and modified PIP coverage requirements, resulting in a $35.0 million reduction to earned premiums recorded in the fourth quarter of 2025 to account for excess profits over a three-year period. Additionally, Kemper faces pending litigation arising from ordinary course operations, including claims handling practices claims seeking bad faith and extra-contractual damages, some of which may pursue class action status. The company experienced a CEO transition during the fiscal year. Separately, Kemper announced an asset sale in 2025 and took a $21.7 million impairment charge on internal-use software assets in the same period, following a $49.6 million goodwill impairment related to its Preferred Property & Casualty Insurance business in 2023.

Kemper's competitive position carries structural vulnerabilities tied to geography and regulation. The company has significant concentration in California and Florida personal automobile insurance, making it exposed to catastrophic loss events in disaster-prone areas and to state-specific regulatory actions like the Florida reforms. The specialty auto segment faces regulatory restrictions on rate increases in certain states and pricing inadequacies from time lag between rate approval and implementation. The Life Insurance segment operates with a higher expense load than the life insurance industry average and serves a customer base with higher lapse ratios than other demographic segments. These factors underscore exposure to both natural disaster risk and regulatory constraint in two of the company's largest markets.

No revenue or earnings guidance has been provided. Capital expenditure plans and named strategic initiatives are not disclosed in the available data.

### OI
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/812074/000110465926014319/oi-20251231x10k.htm)_

_Triggers: $445M impairment disclosed; 1 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; 2 regulatory action(s) disclosed._

O-I Glass, Inc. is a global glass container manufacturer with 64 plants across 18 countries, organized into Americas and Europe segments. The company serves beverage, food, pharmaceutical, and specialty markets, producing glass containers for beer, spirits, wine, soft drinks, juices, teas, and pharmaceuticals. Revenue declined 1.6% to $6.43 billion in fiscal 2025, while the company reported net loss of $129 million. O-I positions itself as a leading glass container manufacturer in most of its operating countries, leveraging its global footprint, manufacturing expertise, and proprietary ULTRA technology that reduces container weight by up to 30%. The company competes against other glass producers including Ardagh Group, Verallia, and Vidrala, as well as manufacturers of alternative packaging such as aluminum cans, plastic containers, and flexible pouches from competitors like Ball Corporation, Crown Holdings, and Amcor.

O-I took a $445 million goodwill impairment charge on its North America reporting unit in 2023 due to lower estimated future cash flows and higher weighted average cost of capital, reflecting structural challenges in the Americas business. During 2025, the company recorded an additional $117 million impairment and restructuring charge related to halting its MAGMA program for modular glass melting furnace development. The company faced $28 million in costs related to European Union Emissions Trading Scheme compliance, where free allocation is being phased out between 2026 and 2034, alongside $5 million in costs from various state, provincial, and municipal carbon pricing requirements. O-I resolved environmental remediation litigation concerning the Cuyahoga River paper mill site with the United States in Q3 2025, paying $16.5 million under a court-approved consent order reached tentatively in Q1 2025.

The company carries significant structural risks. One customer accounts for approximately 10% of consolidated net sales across both Europe and Americas segments, creating meaningful revenue concentration. Energy costs represent 10–20% of manufacturing costs, exposing O-I to substantial volatility in natural gas, fuel oil, and electrical power pricing. The company disclosed substantial goodwill susceptible to future impairment, reflecting prior write-downs. Customer consolidation is creating increased pricing pressures, and seasonal demand variation in beer and beverage products affects operational stability. O-I is executing its Fit to Win initiative through 2026, which includes permanent closure of multiple plants and furnaces in both Americas and Europe announced during 2024–2025. The company completed a new glass container manufacturing plant in Bowling Green, Kentucky in 2024.

O-I plans capital expenditures of $450 million and targets at least $750 million in cumulative Fit to Win benefits through 2027. The company is pursuing a 40% renewable electricity use target by 2030 as part of its sustainability initiatives. No revenue or earnings guidance was provided in the filing.

DENTSPLY SIRONA Inc. designs, manufactures, and sells a broad portfolio of dental and specialty healthcare products across four segments. Connected Technology Solutions encompasses Equipment & Instruments and CAD/CAM offerings. Essential Dental Solutions comprises endodontic, restorative, and preventive consumables and small equipment. Orthodontic and Implant Solutions covers digital implant systems, implant products, digital dentures, and orthodontic solutions. Wellspect Healthcare, a separate segment, develops continence care products for urinary and bowel management. The company operates primarily in the United States and Europe, with secondary exposure to Rest of World markets. DENTSPLY SIRONA positions itself on a 139-year history of innovation, an end-to-end portfolio across dental categories, well-established brand names, and a global sales force and distribution network. The company emphasizes cloud-enabled digital workflow solutions through its DS Core platform and a commitment to quality and professional support. Revenue declined 3% to $3.68 billion in the most recent fiscal year from $3.79 billion in the prior year, with gross margin at 50%.

DENTSPLY SIRONA recorded $525 million in goodwill impairment charges and $125 million in intangible asset impairment charges during fiscal 2025, representing material write-downs of balance sheet value. These impairments follow a $187 million charge in 2024 related to the Byte aligner business, where sales and marketing were suspended in October 2024. The company faces a pending securities class action lawsuit stemming from an internal investigation announced in May 2022 regarding certain financial reporting matters; the SEC investigation has since closed. Additionally, German tax authorities are conducting a criminal investigation into intercompany loans from 2016 and 2017, though no charges had been filed as of the filing date. The company announced a joint venture with Patterson Dental Holdings effective in 2026.

DENTSPLY SIRONA operates with significant customer concentration, with Henry Schein, Inc. and Patterson Companies, Inc. each representing over 10% of revenue. This reliance on a limited number of distributors creates dependency risk, particularly given that Patterson is both a major customer and the counterparty to the announced 2026 joint venture. Supply chain operations depend on sourcing from China and Europe. The company faces ongoing pressure from dental practice consolidation driving price competition, rapid technological disruption across dental markets, and competitors introducing lower-priced alternatives. Two manufacturing facilities in Israel supporting implant products remain operational.

DENTSPLY SIRONA plans capital expenditures in the range of $125 million to $150 million, with a midpoint of approximately $137.5 million. Key initiatives include global ERP system implementation, expansion of the DS Core platform with AI-powered diagnostics capabilities, and a 2026 Plan targeting $120 million in annualized cost savings. The company is also increasing R&D investment to 5% of net sales and has renewed its Patterson Dental distribution agreement.

### EGBN

EAGLE BANCORP INC operates as a community bank through EagleBank, its Maryland-chartered subsidiary, serving the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area, suburban Maryland, and Northern Virginia. The company provides commercial loans, real estate loans, construction and development financing, consumer loans, deposit services, investment securities, treasury management services, online and mobile banking, and SBA lending. Revenue declined 3.1% to $299.2 million in the most recent fiscal year from $308.6 million in the prior year, and the company reported a net loss of $138.1 million. EAGLE BANCORP positions itself as a relationship-focused institution emphasizing superior personalized service, local decision-making, and effective lending for small and medium-sized businesses. The company maintains SBA Preferred Lender Program status and benefits from established relationships with local businesses and professionals across its core markets.

EAGLE BANCORP recognized a $104.2 million goodwill impairment in fiscal 2024, reflecting a material write-down of acquired intangible value. Separately, the company faces a pending investigation by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania, for which it accrued $10 million in provisions subsequent to its January 21, 2026 earnings release. Additionally, EAGLE BANCORP is subject to an FDIC special assessment initiated in March 2023 to recover losses from the systemic risk exception used in the Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank receiverships. These three items—the impairment, the criminal investigation provision, and the regulatory assessment—represent significant headwinds to profitability and shareholder value.

EAGLE BANCORP faces structural constraints relative to larger competitors. The company discloses substantially lower financial resources than large institutions, less extensive branch networks, lower lending capacity due to capitalization limits, and reduced investment capability in technology. The company explicitly identifies concentrated geographic exposure to the Washington D.C. market area as a disadvantage. Competitive pressures arise from large and regional banks operating outside the region, credit unions (which operate on a tax-exempt basis), fintech lenders, internet-based competitors, and nontraditional financial service providers. The company cannot directly offer certain services such as international banking and trust, limiting its ability to serve clients with those needs.

The company provided no revenue or earnings guidance for forward periods and disclosed no capital expenditure plans or named strategic initiatives in the filing.

### HTZ
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1657853/000165785326000008/htz-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: $1.0B+ impairment disclosed; litigation with disclosed exposure $346M+; planned capex $9.4B next fiscal year._

Hertz Global Holdings operates a global vehicle rental business across two segments: Americas RAC and International RAC. The company generated $8.5 billion in revenue for the latest fiscal year, representing a 6% decline from $9.0 billion in the prior year, alongside a net loss of $703 million. The business spans the United States and Europe as primary markets, with secondary operations in Canada, Australia, Latin America, the Caribbean, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and New Zealand. Hertz competes through multiple brands—Hertz, Dollar, and Thrifty—positioning itself at different price points and operating an extensive network of company-owned and franchised rental locations. The core offering encompasses vehicle rentals on various terms, used vehicle sales through its Hertz Car Sales brand, damage waivers and insurance products, premium roadside service, supplemental equipment rentals, fueling and electric charging services, and the Hertz Gold+ loyalty program, which accounts for 33% of transactions. The company also offers ride-share vehicle rentals and a Rent2Buy program.

The 2024 filing discloses material impairments totaling $1.048 billion, split between long-lived assets ($1.048 billion) and an additional $223 million in incremental net depreciation related to a decision to significantly reduce the global EV fleet following asset sales. A settled litigation matter with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association required a $346 million payment made in January 2026 related to a stipulated settlement. Bankruptcy-related litigation remains pending with $24 million in interest expense recognized in 2025. The company also completed $200 million in asset sales during 2025. These events reflect significant balance sheet stress and operational challenges that materialized during the period.

Structural headwinds shape the business substantially. Hertz operates in an intensely competitive market against Avis Budget Group, Enterprise Holdings, and SIXT, alongside ride-share companies, peer-to-peer car sharing platforms, and online travel intermediaries. The company explicitly discloses exposure to residual value risk on non-program vehicles, reliance on third-party distribution channels for significant revenues, and dependency on airport concession agreements with fixed obligations. Seasonal demand concentration in the second and third quarters, coupled with exposure to travel demand fluctuations and economic cycles, creates earnings volatility. The company also faces customer loyalty pressure shifting toward internet travel intermediaries and vulnerability to vehicle supply chain disruptions.

Hertz has committed $9.4 billion in capex for the next fiscal year, centered on fleet refresh initiatives intended to reduce capital costs and strengthen residual values. The company is expanding its Hertz Car Sales e-commerce platform with Amazon Autos integration and rolling out the Rent2Buy program to 25 or more states. Financing initiatives include extending HVF III securitization facilities through 2031 and extending the First Lien RCF to March 2028 for $1.7 billion in commitments.

### KOP
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1315257/000131525726000012/kop-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: 2 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; 2 regulatory action(s) disclosed; CFO changed during fiscal year._

Koppers Holdings Inc. operates three distinct business segments serving specialized industrial end-markets. Revenue declined 10.2% to $1.88 billion in the most recent fiscal year from $2.09 billion previously, with gross margin compressing to 24%. The Railroad and Utility Products and Services segment supplies pressure-treated railroad ties, utility poles, and rail joint bars to North American and Australian markets. Performance Chemicals manufactures wood preservation chemicals including copper-based preservatives and fire-retardant products for residential, industrial, and agricultural applications. Carbon Materials and Chemicals produces creosote, carbon pitch, naphthalene, and carbon black feedstock through coal tar distillation. The company positions itself as the largest supplier of railroad crossties to Class I railroads in North America, the second-largest U.S. utility pole producer, and the largest global supplier of creosote to the North American railroad industry. Koppers claims competitive advantages through vertical integration—particularly in creosote and copper manufacturing—and a national network of treating plants with direct rail access.

The company faces material headwinds across multiple dimensions. Pending litigation includes multiple toxic tort claims alleging illnesses and property damage from exposure to coal tar pitch, benzene, and wood treatment chemicals, alongside environmental liability disputes. The company also faces potential indemnification disputes with Beazer East and Beazer Limited arising from a 1988 asset purchase agreement covering pre-closing environmental and product liability claims. Regulatory pressures are mounting internationally: the Koppers Nyborg facility in Europe must report scope 1 emissions under the EU Emissions Trading System beginning 2025, with anticipated enrollment and gradual allowance reductions by 2028. In Australia, the company must report greenhouse gas emissions and energy use under the National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting Scheme, with potential application of the Safeguard Mechanism if thresholds are exceeded. The company also completed a change in chief financial officer during the fiscal year.

Koppers' operating structure carries several material constraints. The coal tar distillation industry operates in excess capacity, creating pricing pressure and intensifying competition for limited North American and European coal tar supplies. The RUPS business depends heavily on long-term contracts with Class I railroads (approximately 75% of sales), while the Performance Chemicals business supplies ten of the eleven largest U.S. lumber treating companies and four of five largest Canadian firms—creating substantial customer concentration risk. Supply chain vulnerabilities include dependence on hundreds of small sawmills for hardwood lumber, scrap copper purchases of approximately 30 million pounds annually, and reliance on coal tar as the primary raw material for CMC operations across North America and Europe. The company acknowledges inability to pass increased raw material and operating costs to customers and exposure to commodity price fluctuations in copper and coal tar.

Capital allocation plans total $55 million in planned capex. The company is executing a restructuring strategy involving discontinuation of phthalic anhydride production at its Stickney, Illinois facility (completed in Q2 2025), idling of the Vance, Alabama utility products facility in February 2026 with transition to Kennedy, and planned idling of the Florence, South Carolina railroad products facility by November 2026 with production shifted to Guthrie, Kentucky. Koppers completed acquisitions of Brown Wood in 2024 and Greenhill in 2025, as well as an asset sale in 2025.

### IIPR
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1677576/000167757626000001/iipr-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: going concern language present; 2 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; regulatory action: SEC._

INNOVATIVE INDUSTRIAL PROPERTIES INC operates as a landlord to state-licensed cannabis operators and, more recently, as an investor in life science companies. The Cannabis Portfolio Segment leases real estate assets—cultivation facilities, processing operations, and dispensaries—to regulated cannabis operators across 19 states, with primary exposure in Florida, Illinois, Massachusetts, Michigan, and Pennsylvania. The Life Science Portfolio Segment comprises preferred equity and credit facility investments in life science companies. Revenue declined 13.8% to $266.0 million in the most recent fiscal year from $308.5 million in the prior year, though net income was $118.2 million. The company competes against other real estate investors, hedge funds, REITs, independent investors, and cannabis operators themselves, positioning itself on experienced management, recurring contractual rent with escalations, rigorous underwriting, triple-net lease structures, and portfolio diversification. However, the company discloses substantial structural disadvantages: federal cannabis illegality creates legal uncertainty, tenant financial distress poses collection risk, cannabis product pricing is declining, illicit markets limit tenant profitability, and properties specialized for cannabis have limited alternative uses.

The filing carries significant headwinds from regulatory and litigation exposure. An SEC formal investigation commenced in 2026 following subpoena issuance by the Division of Enforcement's Denver Regional Office concerning matters similar to those alleged in pending securities class action lawsuits against the company and certain executive officers for alleged false or misleading statements regarding the business. Derivative lawsuits are also pending against officers and directors asserting breach of fiduciary duty, unjust enrichment, abuse of control, gross mismanagement, and waste of corporate assets. Going concern language appears in the filing, indicating substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern. In 2025, the company recorded a $3.5 million impairment loss on a California property sold in June and regained possession of four California properties through deed in lieu of foreclosure in September 2025, while also recovering possession of a Dwight, Illinois facility through judgment in December 2025—events reflecting tenant defaults and operational stress.

Tenant concentration creates material revenue vulnerability. The top ten tenants collectively represent 75% of total contractual rent collected, with Ascend Wellness Holdings representing 13%, Green Thumb Industries 10%, and both Curaleaf Holdings and Trulieve at 9% each. Properties are specialized for cannabis use with limited conversion potential, and geographic concentration in cannabis-regulated states creates vulnerability to state-level regulatory changes and market dynamics. The company's debt maturity structure poses refinancing risk, with Notes due in May 2026 requiring refinancing. In 2025, the company completed a $50.0 million asset purchase from IQHQ REIT and affiliates, a $100.0 million credit facility joint venture with the same counterparty, and divested three properties for $11.3 million aggregate proceeds.

The company plans to complete a $120.0 million remaining preferred stock investment in IQHQ by June 2027, refresh its tenant base toward more financially stable long-term operators, refinance its 2026 Notes, and develop two properties under redevelopment in California and Texas. No revenue or earnings guidance has been provided.

### EXPI

eXp World Holdings, Inc. operates as a cloud-based real estate brokerage serving residential and commercial markets across North America and 27 international countries. The company generated $4.77 billion in revenue for fiscal 2024, representing 4.5% growth from the prior year, though this top-line expansion masked underlying margin pressure—gross margin stood at 7.0% and operating margin turned slightly negative at negative 0.4%, resulting in a net loss of $22.7 million. The business is organized into three segments: North American Realty, which includes U.S. and Canadian brokerage operations plus lead generation services and, beginning Q1 2025, the FrameVR.io 3D immersive platform acquired during the year; International Realty, encompassing brokerage operations across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Asia-Pacific, and South Africa; and Other Affiliated Services, which publishes SUCCESS® magazine and related media for agent training and support. The company positions itself as the only global cloud-based real estate brokerage offering what it describes as industry-leading economics, low agent entry fees, stock ownership opportunities, and a revenue-sharing multi-tiered compensation structure designed to attract and retain agents.

The company faces material legal and regulatory headwinds stemming from industry-wide antitrust scrutiny. In December 2024, eXp World settled a nationwide antitrust class action (1925 Hooper LLC, et al. v. The National Association of Realtors et al., Case No. 1:23-cv-05392-SEG) for $34 million, resolving all antitrust claims against the company. However, the company remains a named defendant in separate pending class action suits alleging conspiracy to violate federal antitrust laws regarding inflated commission fees. This litigation activity must be viewed in context of broader industry disruption: the National Association of Realtors reached a $418 million settlement in March 2024 requiring elimination of buyer broker compensation mandates on Multiple Listing Services and implementation of written buyer agreements—changes that directly alter brokerage economics industry-wide. Additionally, the U.S. Department of Justice reopened its investigation into NAR in April 2024 after a federal appeals court determination, creating continued regulatory uncertainty. In the governance sphere, the company appointed Jesse Hill as Chief Financial Officer in Q3 2025, Carrie Lysenko as Chief Technology Officer of eXp Realty in Q4 2025, and Holly Mabery as Chief Brokerage Officer of eXp Realty in Q4 2025. The company also completed impairment charges of $4.93 million related to its other affiliated services segment in fiscal 2024 and wound down and completed disposition of its Virbela business in the fourth quarter of 2024.

The business operates with significant structural vulnerabilities. The company explicitly discloses exposure to cyclical residential real estate markets, dependence on U.S. Federal Reserve monetary policies and mortgage interest rates, vulnerability to housing inventory fluctuations, and subject exposure to declining commission rates from competitive pressures and antitrust litigation. A critical dependency exists on third-party cloud platform vendors for essential infrastructure, and the company faces stated challenges in agent and broker recruitment and retention amid industry changes. The extremely thin 7.0% gross margin and negative operating margin reflect the capital-intensive nature of scaling cloud infrastructure while competing against local brokerages with strong brand recognition and discount brokers with reduced operating cost structures. The company also acknowledges regulatory scrutiny of its revenue-sharing plan and network marketing structure as an ongoing concern.

The company launched several new business units and platform initiatives during 2024–2025: a Land and Ranch Division in Q2 2025, a Sports and Entertainment Division in Q4 2025, a CRM of Choice platform in Q3 2025 enabling agent selection, and the LYVVE global property search platform in Q4 2025. International expansion includes planned entry into six new countries—Peru, Ecuador, Türkiye, Japan, Romania, and the Netherlands. The company did not provide revenue

Advance Auto Parts operates as a leading automotive aftermarket retailer across North America, serving professional installers, DIY customers, and independently-owned operators through its Advance Auto Parts and Carquest branded stores. The company carries Parts & Batteries, Accessories & Chemicals, and Engine Maintenance products across 4,305 stores in the United States, Canada, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Mexico, and Caribbean islands, with the U.S. market representing its primary geography. Revenue declined 5.4% to $8.6 billion in the most recent fiscal year from $9.1 billion, though gross margin remained solid at 43.4%. The company positions itself on broad product selection, extensive geographic reach, multi-echelon supply chain capabilities enabling same-day or next-day parts availability, omnichannel offerings including e-commerce and mobile platforms, and a loyal customer base across both professional and DIY segments.

A $431 million inventory write-down in 2024 related to restructuring liquidation sales and streamlining activities reflects substantial operational contraction. The company completed the sale of its Worldpac business in November 2024 for $1.44 billion in net proceeds and closed approximately 500 stores and 200 independent locations during Q1 2025 under its 2024 Restructuring Plan, alongside closure of four distribution centers by mid-2025. Additional impairments totaling $56 million were recorded in 2024 and 2025 for right-of-use assets and property and equipment tied to restructuring. The company also faces two pending litigation matters: a securities class action regarding past public disclosures with related derivative shareholder litigation following a significant stock price decline, and numerous asbestos exposure injury lawsuits. A $28 million expected credit loss on vendor receivables was recorded in 2025 stemming from a vendor bankruptcy.

Advance Auto Parts operates with material structural constraints. The company faces significant indebtedness that the extraction identifies as limiting operational flexibility, alongside exposure to rising competitive pressure from national chains like AutoZone, O'Reilly Automotive, and NAPA, as well as internet-based retailers benefiting from lower overhead costs. The company purchases from over 730 vendors with no disclosed concentration threshold, but remains dependent on suppliers subject to tariffs and supply chain disruptions. A stated disadvantage highlights exposure to declining vehicle maintenance demand driven by electric vehicle adoption. Operating margin turned negative at negative 0.5% despite the 43.4% gross margin, underscoring the weight of operating expenses in the current restructuring environment.

Advance Auto Parts plans approximately $300 million in capital expenditures for fiscal 2026 focused on store infrastructure upgrades. Key initiatives include distribution network optimization converting facilities to market hubs, supply chain transformation to drive operational efficiencies, and the January 2026 launch of ARGOS, an owned brand targeting high-quality affordable auto care products. Restructuring expenses are estimated at $30 million to $40 million through fiscal 2026. No revenue or earnings per share guidance has been provided.

### HOG

Harley-Davidson manufactures and sells motorcycles, parts, accessories, apparel and licensed products through its flagship Harley-Davidson Motor Company (HDMC) segment, which operates a global dealer network spanning the United States, Canada, EMEA, Asia Pacific, and Latin America. The company also operates LiveWire, an all-electric motorcycle brand offering two-wheel electric motorcycles, electric balance bikes for children, e-bikes and related apparel in U.S. and select international markets. A third segment, Harley-Davidson Financial Services (HDFS), provides wholesale inventory financing, retail consumer loans, insurance services and captive reinsurance primarily for Harley-Davidson and LiveWire motorcycles. Revenue declined 13.2% to $3.6 billion in the fiscal year, with gross margin contracting to 24.2% and operating margin turning negative at negative 0.8%, though net income remained positive at $339 million.

The company disclosed a pending investigation by Japan's Fair Trade Commission into Harley-Davidson Japan KK for alleged improper conduct including setting excessive sales quotas for motorcycle dealers. This matter remains unresolved with no quantified financial exposure. Additionally, Harley-Davidson completed an asset sale to KKR and PIMCO for $46.6 million in 2025. The filing also reflects a CEO change during the fiscal year, signaling a transition in executive leadership.

Harley-Davidson's competitive positioning is built on premium pricing, distinctive brand heritage dating to 1903, and a comprehensive financial services offering through HDFS. However, the company operates with structural headwinds: its higher suggested retail prices create vulnerability against competitors, it faces pricing pressure from international manufacturers with currency advantages, and it depends entirely on an independent dealer network for retail distribution. The business carries exposure to credit risk on retail and wholesale finance receivables. Supply chain concentration in Thailand for certain Asian and European models, Brazil for assembly operations, and Taiwan and China for STACYC electric balance bike manufacturing creates vulnerability to geopolitical and logistics disruptions. Tariff impacts on raw materials and finished motorcycles also constrain margins.

Capital expenditures are planned in the $175 million to $200 million range, with $187.5 million as the midpoint. Key initiatives include launching a new small displacement motorcycle and an iconic classic cruiser model both starting in 2026, shifting annual model year launch timing to fall, launching LiveWire mini-motorcycles production, and announcing a new strategic plan in Q2 2026. ### PRAA
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1185348/000118534826000006/praa-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: $413M impairment disclosed; 1 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; 1 regulatory action(s) disclosed._

PRA GROUP INC purchases and collects nonperforming loans across 18 countries, operating through two primary segments: a U.S. business and a European business spanning 12 countries plus the UK. The company also pursues insolvency accounts and class action claims recovery services. Revenue grew 7.8% to $1.2 billion in fiscal 2025 from $1.1 billion in the prior year. However, the company reported a net loss of $305 million, driven largely by a $413 million goodwill impairment charge on its Debt Buying and Collection reporting unit tied to a sustained decrease in stock price and market capitalization. The operating margin turned negative at -2.5%, reflecting the impairment's impact on profitability. PRA GROUP positions itself competitively through diverse global presence, longstanding relationships with credit originators, strong capital position, an extensive proprietary data set for underwriting, and a comprehensive compliance program.

The $413 million goodwill impairment signals material valuation pressure and reflects market skepticism about near-term recovery in the business. Additionally, PRA GROUP's subsidiary Portfolio Recovery Associates, LLC settled a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigation into debt collection practices through an April 2023 order; the company is executing a compliance plan under that settlement. The CFPB continues to issue civil investigative demands and periodically examines the company's debt collection practices. These regulatory actions underscore heightened scrutiny of the company's collection methodology and compliance obligations going forward. The company also completed an asset sale to RCB Investimentos S.A. in 2025.

The business carries structural vulnerabilities that warrant investor attention. Nonperforming loans are inherently difficult to collect, and the company may not recover sufficient amounts to justify its investment. Operations depend on third-party service providers for collection activities and on internally developed models that may prove inaccurate. The portfolio purchasing cadence is variable by quarter and year, creating revenue volatility. Regulatory complexity burdens the U.S. business, while Europe's diverse regulatory environments create uneven competitive dynamics. Consumer economic downturns directly threaten collection rates and recoveries. The company faces competition from other debt purchasers on price, reputation, and long-term performance.

Looking forward, PRA GROUP is strengthening its U.S. platform through call center consolidation and offshore expansion, expanding its legal collections channel across U.S. and European markets, and standardizing technology infrastructure with AI deployment for operational efficiency. The company completed a €300 million Euro-denominated senior notes issuance in September 2025 and is pursuing selective portfolio purchasing focused on long-term returns and leverage management. No specific revenue or earnings guidance has been provided.

Albany International Corp /DE/ is a diversified manufacturer operating two primary segments: Machine Clothing, positioned as the world's leading producer of custom-designed fabrics and high-speed process belts for paper manufacturing, and Albany Engineered Composites, a leader in advanced composite technology for aerospace and defense applications. The company serves North America, Europe, and Asia as primary markets, with secondary exposure to South America. Revenue declined 3.9% to $1.18 billion in fiscal 2025, while the company posted a net loss of $57 million with an operating margin of negative 3.1% and gross margin of 20.6%. Within Machine Clothing, the company offers Paper Machine Clothing and Engineered Fabric products for nonwovens, fiber cement, and industrial applications. Albany Engineered Composites manufactures advanced composite fan blades, fan cases, and components for commercial and defense markets, and serves as the exclusive supplier of advanced composite fan blades and cases for the LEAP engine, with SAFRAN accounting for approximately 15% of consolidated net revenues in 2025.

Albany International took a $165.8 million impairment charge in fiscal 2025 primarily related to the CH-53K program within the Engineered Composites segment, driven by greater-than-planned labor content and higher material inputs on a long-term contract. The company is named as a defendant in pending litigation relating to asbestos-containing products, with no disclosed financial exposure quantified. Separately, the U.S. Department of War certified Albany Engineered Composites' Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification at Level 2 in December 2025, a requirement for defense contracts. The impairment, combined with operational headwinds, reflects execution challenges on fixed-price aerospace contracts and ongoing restructuring efforts.

The company faces structural headwinds in its Machine Clothing segment from significant consolidation and rationalization in the paper industry, reduced newsprint and printing paper demand driven by digital media, and a shift from traditional corrugated boxes to alternative packaging formats. Chinese competitors and domestic manufacturer preferences in China limit competitiveness in that market. Within Engineered Composites, the company confronts aerospace industry consolidation, highly competitive and price-sensitive markets, and competitors with greater manufacturing and financial resources. Supply chain risks exist around limited suppliers of critical raw materials including carbon fiber and polymer monofilaments, though the company sources approximately 20% of worldwide monofilament requirements from an internal facility in Homer, New York. SAFRAN concentration at 15% of revenue creates customer dependency, particularly given the fixed-price nature of long-term aerospace contracts, as evidenced by the CH-53K charge.

Albany International is executing a multi-year Heimbach integration program with footprint realignment, having completed closures of facilities in South Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, and announced closures in Italy, France, and the United Kingdom during 2025. The company completed the sale of its Arcari business in 2025 and announced a strategic review of its structures assembly business at the Salt Lake City facility, with divestiture pending. Headquarters consolidation to Portsmouth, New Hampshire is targeted for completion in the first half of 2026. The company is developing 3D-woven technology for aerospace and defense applications and anticipates New Business Ventures revenue growth by 2027. No revenue or earnings guidance was provided.

### RUN
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1469367/000162828026012289/run-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: $3.1B+ impairment disclosed; 2 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; 1 regulatory action(s) disclosed._

Sunrun Inc. designs, installs, owns and maintains residential solar and battery storage systems across the United States, operating primarily through customer agreements structured as leases and power purchase agreements alongside direct sales. Revenue grew 45% to $3.0 billion in the most recent fiscal year from $2.0 billion in the prior period. The company operates a single reportable segment focused on residential solar and storage and holds the largest fleet of residential energy systems in the United States. Its stated competitive advantages include multi-channel sales and installation capabilities, proprietary technology platforms, predictable 20-25 year customer contracts, and battery storage offerings. The company positions itself as moving toward a storage-first model and largest home-to-grid operator.

Sunrun recorded a $3.1 billion goodwill impairment charge in the fourth quarter of 2024 following a quantitative impairment assessment, driven primarily by a decline in market capitalization that caused the fair value of the reporting unit to fall below carrying value. Two pending litigation matters have been disclosed: a lawsuit filed by Puerto Rico's Fiscal Oversight and Management Board in 2024 challenging net metering policy, which could revise or reverse the current net metering extension through 2031, and a prior administrative proceeding settled with the California Contractors State License Board. Additionally, California's Contractors State License Board adopted a new rule effective October 1, 2024 requiring C-10 licenses for energy storage system repair and retrofit work; enforcement is currently enjoined pending case resolution.

The business faces meaningful structural constraints. Over 45% of the customer base concentrates in California, and the company explicitly discloses that California's net metering policy changes have reduced financial attractiveness of its offerings there. Supply chains depend on a limited number of manufacturers for solar panels, inverters and batteries, with particular exposure to China for lithium-ion battery cells and Vietnam for component sourcing subject to tariffs and trade restrictions. The shift from leasing toward outright customer purchases is reshaping the business model. Gross margin stands at 31.5% against an operating margin of negative 4.3%, with reported net loss of $1.0 billion in the fiscal year, reflecting the substantial impairment charge and operational dynamics.

The company is pursuing grid services expansion through distributed power plants, home electrification offerings including EV chargers and battery retrofits, and strategic acquisitions of previously installed solar systems. It remains focused on California's solar-plus-storage market under the net billing tariff framework. No revenue or earnings guidance has been provided.

### UCTT
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1275014/000162828026010744/uctt-20251226.htm)_

_Triggers: 2 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; regulatory action: SEC; CEO changed during fiscal year._

Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. designs, engineers and manufactures production tools, components and parts for the semiconductor and display capital equipment markets through its Products segment, which includes chemical delivery modules, gas delivery systems, fluid delivery systems, precision robotics and process modules. The company also operates a Services segment providing ultra-high purity parts cleaning, process tool part recoating and micro-contamination analysis primarily for semiconductor device makers and wafer fabrication equipment customers. Ultra Clean maintains a primary presence in Asia Pacific and Europe and Middle East, with secondary operations in the United States. Revenue declined 2.1% to $2.054 billion in fiscal 2025, while gross margin compressed to 15.7% and the company posted a negative operating margin of negative 5.2%, reflecting significant operational challenges during the period.

The company faces material headwinds from two separate litigation matters and a regulatory investigation that underscore governance and disclosure concerns. A putative securities class action was filed in U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on March 24, 2025 and subsequently dismissed, while a derivative suit against the Board of Directors was filed in Superior Court of California, County of Alameda on August 1, 2025 and also dismissed. More substantively, the SEC issued a subpoena in 2024 related to material weaknesses identified in the company's 2022 and 2023 annual reports and the change of independent auditors. The company also recorded a $77.6 million goodwill impairment in its Fluid Solutions reporting unit within the Products segment and a $73.5 million goodwill impairment in the Services reporting unit during fiscal 2025. Additionally, a factoring agreement for the Fluid Solutions business was cancelled in December 2025. Leadership transitioned during the fiscal year as the CEO changed, though the CFO and auditor (PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP) remained in place.

Ultra Clean's competitive position rests on vertical integration, local presence near customer facilities and over 30 years of experience in complex gas delivery systems, but the business carries acute concentration risk. Applied Materials, Inc. and Lam Research Corporation each accounted for more than 10% of revenue in fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023, with the top two customers representing 58.7% of total revenues in the current year. The company explicitly discloses that customers own designs and intellectual property for manufactured products, can license designs to competitors, may develop internal manufacturing capabilities, and can shift to in-house cleaning and coating services. Competition comes from specialized suppliers including Ichor Systems, Fujikin Incorporated and Foxsemicon Integrated Technology Inc., as well as larger diversified manufacturers like Jabil and Celestica, plus customers' own internal capabilities. The company also notes it faces competition from suppliers with greater financial and technical resources and faces cyclical semiconductor demand volatility.

The company is pursuing a new enterprise resource planning system implementation, vertical integration expansion through acquisitions along the semiconductor supply chain, selective geographic expansion in lower-cost manufacturing regions and services business market share growth with IDM and foundry customers. No revenue or earnings guidance was provided. The company operates facilities in areas with elevated seismic activity, including Hayward, California and Taiwan.

### NX
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1423221/000142322125000100/nx-20251031.htm)_

_Triggers: material weakness in internal controls disclosed; $302M impairment disclosed; 2 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed._

Quanex Building Products manufactures components and systems for window, door, and building products across three segments: Hardware Solutions (window and door hardware and screens), Extruded Solutions (insulating glass spacers, vinyl profiles, seals, and weatherstripping), and Custom Solutions (wood, mixing, and building access products). The company serves North America and the United Kingdom as primary markets, with secondary operations in Germany, Mexico, Italy, Canada, and broader Europe. Revenue grew 43.8% to $1.84 billion in the most recent period, driven substantially by the completed $504 million acquisition of Tyman plc in 2024. However, the company reported a net loss of $251 million, with gross margin at 27.1% and operating margin deteriorating to negative 10.6%, reflecting integration costs and market headwinds. Quanex positions itself on cost-effective production, engineering expertise, design capability, high-quality manufacturing, just-in-time delivery, and proprietary technology around vinyl extrusion and spacer designs protected by patents.

The $302 million goodwill impairment charge recorded in Q3 2025 signals material pressure on the Tyman acquisition value. The company attributes the write-down to segment restructuring triggered by prolonged stock price decline driven by weaker consumer confidence and industry uncertainty. Of this amount, $44.8 million is tax-deductible; the remainder is not. Additionally, Quanex disclosed a material weakness in internal controls and confirmed that disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting are not effective. A purported shareholder class action (Zanol v. Quanex Building Products Corporation et al, Case No. 4:25-cv-04453) alleges violations of federal securities laws related to public disclosures made in 2025 concerning window and door operations in Mexico, with unspecified damages sought. The company is also defending multiple remaining claims related to alleged defects in a commercial sealant product manufactured and sold in the 2000s; several claims have been resolved, and the company believes it would prevail if remaining claims proceed to trial.

Quanex operates in a highly concentrated customer environment. The company disclosed that certain businesses and product lines are largely dependent on relatively few large customers, and that primary customers are OEMs with substantial pricing leverage. This concentration is compounded by the risk that customers may vertically integrate operations or diversify their supplier base. The competitive landscape is fragmented but includes larger players such as Assa Abloy, Veka, and Roto, alongside mid-size suppliers and smaller window manufacturers. Supply-side constraints present operational friction: the company operates in rural areas with a limited qualified labor pool and faces exposure to supply chain disruptions and raw material scarcity. The cyclical nature of the housing and remodeling markets adds demand volatility.

The company is pursuing integration of the Tyman acquisition and cross-selling opportunities across the combined platform, alongside restructuring of reporting segments to reflect the new operational alignment. Quanex is also pursuing mitigation of tariff and global trade policy exposure through supplier strategies and seeking to participate in European energy efficiency retrofit programs. No revenue or earnings guidance was provided.

### CABO
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1632127/000163212726000005/cabo-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: $497M impairment disclosed; 1 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; CEO changed during fiscal year._

Cable One, Inc. operates as an integrated broadband communications provider delivering data, video, and voice services across 24 Western, Midwestern, and Southern states with primary operations in Arizona, Idaho, Mississippi, Missouri, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas. The company reported revenue of $1.50 billion in fiscal 2025, declining 4.9% from $1.58 billion in the prior year. Revenue contraction reflects headwinds across both residential and business segments, driven by competitive pressures and cord-cutting trends in video services. Cable One positions itself on infrastructure quality and cost efficiency, citing its fiber-based and hybrid fiber-coaxial network with Gigabit speeds available to all passings and multi-Gigabit service deployed in 53% of markets, supported by low operating cost structures and deep customer relationships in non-metropolitan markets.

The fiscal 2025 filing discloses two impairments totaling $586 million that fundamentally reshape the balance sheet. Cable One recognized a $497 million impairment of indefinite-lived franchise agreements intangible assets triggered by stock price decline, intensifying competition, and reduced estimated cash flows. A follow-on $88.8 million goodwill impairment resulted from the downward fair value reassessment. Additionally, the company is defending pending litigation alleging intellectual property infringement in network infrastructure, system architecture, and modem technology, along with civil claims including contract disputes and wage-and-hour violations; no financial exposure is quantified. The CEO changed during the fiscal year, signaling potential management transition amid operational challenges. Cable One has committed to acquire the remaining equity interests in MBI for $480 million, with closing expected October 1, 2026, and has disclosed a pending asset sale to Point Broadband Holdings, LLC.

Cable One faces structural headwinds that limit pricing power and growth. Nearly 60% of its service footprint is already overbuilt by wired competitors, and the company explicitly identifies rising competition from telephone companies deploying DSL or fiber, regional fiber providers, 5G fixed wireless access providers, and government-subsidized broadband deployments under RDOF, ARPA, and the Infrastructure Act. Video service demand is eroding due to over-the-top platforms including Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, YouTube TV, and others, while rising programming costs and retransmission fees compress video margins. The company reported a negative operating margin of negative 13.8% in fiscal 2025 and net loss of $356 million, heavily influenced by the intangible asset write-downs. Disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting remain effective, and no restatement or going concern language is present.

Cable One is deploying DOCSIS 4.0 technology across markets and rolling out multi-Gigabit download service to additional geographies. A mobile virtual network operator pilot is underway in select markets, and the unified billing platform implementation was completed in 2025. No revenue or earnings guidance has been provided for forward periods.

### FUN
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1999001/000199900126000048/fun-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: $1.5B+ impairment disclosed; 5 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; CEO changed during fiscal year._

Six Flags Entertainment Corporation operates North America's largest regional amusement park portfolio, comprising 26 amusement parks, 15 separately gated water parks, and nine resort properties across the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Revenue grew 14.4% to $3.1 billion in the most recent fiscal year, driven by admissions, food and merchandise sales, accommodations, and extra-charge products. The company positions itself as a more affordable alternative to destination parks for regional guests, leveraging exclusive long-term licensing agreements for Warner Bros., DC Comics, and Peanuts characters alongside internationally recognized brand names including Cedar Point and Knott's Berry Farm. Geographic diversity across top-10 designated market areas and continuous capital investment in new attractions form the core of its competitive strategy.

The filing reflects substantial operational and financial strain in the wake of the July 2024 merger of former Six Flags and Cedar Fair. A $1.52 billion impairment charge was recorded in the third quarter of 2025 against goodwill and intangible assets—including the Former Six Flags and Schlitterbahn reporting units and both associated trade names—stemming from a decline in estimated future cash flows as revenue and earnings underperformed expectations and the company's share price sustained decline. This impairment directly contributed to a net loss of $1.55 billion despite positive revenue growth. CEO changes occurred during the fiscal year, and two directors were appointed by activist investors Dendur Capital LP in March 2025 and one by Sachem Head Capital Management LP in October 2025, signaling investor pressure on management execution. Five pending litigation matters further complicate the landscape: a Canadian Competition Act case alleging deceptive drip pricing practices, a federal securities class action challenging the July 2024 merger registration statement, a shareholder derivative suit asserting breach of fiduciary duty, and two disability accommodation class actions under the Americans with Disabilities Act and state law. None have quantified financial exposure at this stage.

The company's structural vulnerabilities are acute and material. Operating margin deteriorated sharply to negative 44.4%, driven principally by the goodwill impairment but reflective of broader operational headwinds. A high fixed-cost structure makes the business vulnerable to attendance fluctuations, exacerbated by seasonal concentration—70% of revenue occurs in the second and third quarters. Indebtedness of $5.2 billion significantly constrains financial flexibility. Dependence on third-party ride manufacturers with limited supply capacity and reliance on third-party license agreements subject to termination create additional structural risks. The company also disclosed integration challenges stemming from the merger of two independent companies. Portfolio optimization is underway, including the closure of the Bowie, Maryland property at the end of the 2025 operating season and pending completion of Six Flags Over Georgia and White Water Atlanta acquisition in January 2027.

Capital expenditure is planned in the range of $400 million to $425 million. The company is managing Six Flags Qiddiya City and Aquarabia Qiddiya City development initiatives but has provided no revenue or earnings guidance for the forward period.

### WT

_Triggers: 1 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; regulatory action: SEC._

WisdomTree operates as an ETP sponsor and asset manager offering investment advisory services globally through subsidiaries in the U.S. and Europe. The company provides a broad suite of products across U.S. equity, international developed and emerging market equity, fixed income, commodities and currencies, leveraged and inverse, cryptocurrency, alternatives, and private assets. Revenue grew 15.4% to $493.8 million, with gross margin of 81.9% and operating margin of 35.3%, reflecting strong pricing power and operational leverage in its advisory and sponsorship model. WisdomTree positions itself on first-to-market capabilities, proprietary Modern Alpha indexing that blends active and passive management, and self-indexing infrastructure that reduces third-party licensing costs. The company has cultivated an early-mover advantage in digital assets and blockchain-enabled financial services, supported by an established brand and experienced team.

WisdomTree faces two material regulatory and legal headwinds. The company settled an SEC enforcement matter in 2024 regarding ESG screening disclosures for three ETFs advised by WisdomTree Asset Management, Inc., resulting in a $4 million charge. Separately, the company disclosed pending litigation related to WisdomTree WTI Crude Oil 3x Daily Leveraged ETP, with investor claims totaling approximately €23.6 million ($27.8 million), including appealed claims for €15.2 million ($17.9 million) in damages. These matters reflect execution and disclosure risks in product management and marketing.

WisdomTree operates in a highly fragmented competitive landscape dominated by much larger players including iShares, Vanguard, State Street, Invesco, and Fidelity. The company acknowledges material structural disadvantages: smaller scale limiting resources, more constrained distribution channels compared to financial institutions with direct retail or institutional reach, and ongoing fee compression eroding pricing power. Regulatory uncertainty in digital assets poses a business risk, as does WisdomTree's acknowledged limited experience in private asset markets and dependence on third-party service providers for critical functions. The low barrier to entry in ETPs has attracted new competitors that may erode differentiation.

WisdomTree is pursuing aggressive inorganic growth through multiple channels. The company completed a $275 million acquisition of Ceres Partners, LLC to enter private assets and farmland investments, acquired AlphaBeta ETF Ltd for $2.5 million, and announced an asset purchase from Quorus Inc. and a joint venture with Korea Investment Management Co. Ltd. Organic initiatives include expansion of its WisdomTree Connect institutional platform for digital funds, the WisdomTree Treasury Money Market Digital Fund ($733 million AUM), and WisdomTree Prime, a blockchain-native digital wallet launched this period. Portfolio Solutions is targeting $6.1 billion AUA expansion. No revenue or earnings guidance was provided.

### TRN
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/99780/000009978026000014/trn-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: 1 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; planned capex $3.5B next fiscal year._

Trinity Industries operates two primary business segments across North America's rail transportation ecosystem. The Railcar Leasing and Services Group provides operating leases, fleet maintenance, digital services, and logistics solutions for freight and tank railcars, positioning itself as the comprehensive service provider in the market. The Rail Products Group manufactures freight and tank railcars through facilities in the United States and Mexico, offering covered hoppers, open hoppers, gondolas, pressure and non-pressure tank cars, alongside parts distribution and sustainable conversion programs. The company maintains manufacturing and sourcing operations in Mexico while serving primary markets across the U.S., Mexico, and Canada.

Revenue declined 30% to $2.16 billion in the most recent fiscal period from $3.08 billion in the prior year, though the company generated net income of $284.5 million. Operating margin remained substantial at 30.1% despite the gross margin compression to 26.5%, reflecting the challenging demand environment. Trinity Industries retained responsibility for pending litigation related to the ET-Plus® System highway guardrail end-terminal product following the sale of its highway products business. The company also executed asset sales and purchases with Napier Park Railcar Lease Fund LLC in 2025 as part of portfolio management activity. A fire at the Cartersville, Georgia manufacturing facility in 2024 resulted in insurance recoveries that exceeded the net book value of the destroyed assets.

Trinity's structural position reflects exposure to several material constraints. The company depends on at least two suppliers for the majority of specialty components including brakes, wheels, heads, side frames, bolsters, and bearings—a concentration that creates supply chain vulnerability. Demand exhibits cyclicality tied to energy, agriculture, and consumer products sectors, while steel price volatility and labor shortages directly pressure manufacturing economics. The significant portion of manufacturing footprint in Mexico introduces trade risk exposure. Competitive intensity remains high against five major railcar lessors and four major railcar manufacturers alongside numerous smaller providers. The company does claim competitive advantages through its integrated platform, digital transformation leadership, diversified manufacturing capabilities, patent portfolio, and single-source positioning across leasing, manufacturing, and services.

Trinity Industries has committed capital expenditures of $3.5 billion for the next fiscal year, within a range of $3.2 billion to $3.8 billion, alongside net fleet investment of $450 million to $550 million. The company is expanding its Green Financing Framework with over $4 billion in qualifying debt, signaling strategic emphasis on sustainable rail solutions. No revenue or earnings guidance was provided for forward periods.

### MSEX
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/66004/000162828026009777/msex-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: 2 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; auditor changed during fiscal year._

Middlesex Water Co operates two business segments serving New Jersey and Delaware. The Regulated segment collects, treats, and distributes water on a retail and wholesale basis to residential, commercial, industrial, and fire protection customers, and also provides regulated wastewater services in New Jersey. The Non-Regulated segment operates and maintains municipal and private water and wastewater systems under contract across both states. Revenue grew 1.5% to $194.7 million in the most recent period from $191.9 million, with an operating margin of 27.9%. The company positions itself around exclusive franchises for existing community water systems in Delaware, adequate water supply sources for current requirements, and physically separate water supply systems that provide operational flexibility. Management emphasizes established relationships with multiple municipal customers as a competitive advantage.

The company faces two pending litigation matters in the normal course of business, which management believes will not have a material adverse effect on consolidated financial statements. Separately, Middlesex was a defendant in multi-district litigation against PFAS manufacturers including 3M Company, DuPont de Nemours, Inc., Tyco Fire Products LP, and BASF Corporation for damages and reimbursement of costs related to PFAS in public water supplies; that matter has been settled. Additionally, Middlesex changed its auditor during the fiscal year to PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP. The company has completed several acquisitions including the purchase of assets from the Town of Ocean View, Delaware for $4.6 million in 2025 and from Pinewood Acres, LLC for $200,000 in 2026. A merger of Pinelands Water Company and Pinelands Wastewater Company into Middlesex was approved in 2026.

The company's structural position is shaped by meaningful geographic and operational constraints. It operates in a concentrated footprint across central New Jersey and Delaware, and depends on specific water supply sources including untreated surface water from the Delaware & Raritan Canal in New Jersey and treated water purchases from non-affiliated NJBPU-regulated utilities and the City of Dover. Rate-setting is subject to Public Utility Commission approval, limiting pricing flexibility. The company also discloses exposure to drought and aquifer depletion, water contamination risks, weather volatility affecting usage and revenue, supply chain disruptions for chemicals and materials, and the risk that contract operations may incur costs exceeding revenues.

Middlesex plans capital expenditures of $126 million. Key initiatives include integrating PFAS removal at the CJO Plant with a $255 million investment spanning 2026–2028, constructing the Bethany Bay new water treatment facility in Tidewater, executing the RENEW Program for water main replacement in the Middlesex System, building elevated storage tanks in the Tidewater System for $13 million, and replacing transmission mains in Metuchen for $17 million in 2027–2028.

### CPK
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/19745/000162828026011753/cpk-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: 1 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; regulatory action: FERC._

Chesapeake Utilities Corp operates a bifurcated energy delivery business spanning regulated and unregulated segments across the Mid-Atlantic, Florida, and Ohio. The Regulated Energy segment provides natural gas and electric distribution along with natural gas transmission services across Delaware, Maryland, Florida, Ohio, and secondary markets in Pennsylvania, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Virginia. The Unregulated Energy segment encompasses propane operations, unregulated natural gas transmission and supply through Aspire Energy, electricity and steam generation via Eight Flags, and emerging renewable natural gas initiatives including the Full Circle Dairy RNG facility and the Noble Road Landfill RNG project. Revenue grew 18.1% to $930 million, driven in part by the completed $922.8 million acquisition of assets from Florida Power & Light Company in 2023. The company positions itself around an integrated platform of energy delivery businesses, top-tier returns on equity relative to peers, and established regulated utility foundation supporting diversified unregulated growth.

The Florida Supreme Court litigation initiated by the Office of Public Counsel regarding Florida Gas Company's May 2022 rate case continues to advance, with oral arguments held in December 2024 and outcome still pending. Separately, FERC approved the Worcester Resiliency Upgrade project for Eastern Shore in January 2025 with revised initial transportation rates approved in July 2025, unlocking a key midstream infrastructure investment. More broadly, Chesapeake has secured consecutive regulatory wins: the Florida PSC approved a $23.3 million rate increase for FCG and the $205 million GUARD program for safety and infrastructure investment; Maryland and Delaware rate cases settled in 2025 for cumulative annual increases of $3.5 million and $6.1 million respectively; and Florida's FPU electric rate case yielded an $8.6 million annual base rate increase with additional step-up upon project completion. A Florida PSC depreciation study in February 2026 determined a $6.8 million reserve imbalance to be amortized over remaining asset life.

Chesapeake carries concentrated customer dependencies that shape operational risk. Peninsula Pipeline's contracted firm transportation capacity is 99% derived from affiliated local distribution companies, while Eastern Shore's capacity is 52% similarly concentrated. Aspire Energy revenues depend substantially on two customers—Columbia Gas of Ohio and Consumers Gas Cooperative—under long-term supply agreements serving over 23,000 end customers. Eight Flags operates under two separate 20-year contracts with a Florida electric distribution operation and a site customer. The company also discloses reliance on two main pipeline systems in Florida and dependence on Marcellus and Utica production areas for natural gas purchases. Gross margin of 48.7% and operating margin of 27.5% reflect the capital-intensive, regulated-utility-heavy nature of the business. Stated disadvantages include weather sensitivity, capital intensity, regulatory rate approval uncertainties, and exposure to commodity price and supply chain risks.

Capital deployment of $450 million to $500 million is planned, with $475 million as the midpoint. Key initiatives include the Worcester Resiliency Upgrade LNG storage facility completing mid-2026, Miami Inner Loop pipeline projects targeted for second quarter 2026, ongoing Full Circle Dairy RNG operations, expansion of the CNG/RNG/LNG virtual pipeline fleet, and Florida GUARD and FCG SAFE infrastructure programs.

### COLL

Collegium Pharmaceutical is a biopharmaceutical company with a single operating segment focused on ADHD and pain management products for the United States market. Revenue grew 23.6% to $780.6 million in the most recent period from $631.4 million in the prior year, with gross margin of 59.3% and operating margin of 23.0%, generating net income of $62.9 million. The company's portfolio includes Jornay PM, an evening-dosed ADHD stimulant with abuse-deterrent DETERx technology that holds FDA approval as the only evening-dosed stimulant in its category; Xtampza ER and Nucynta ER, extended-release opioid pain products; Belbuca, a buccal film opioid formulation; and Symproic for opioid-induced constipation. The company competes against major multinational firms including Vertex, Novartis, J&J Innovative Medicines, and Supernus Pharmaceuticals, as well as generic manufacturers. Collegium positions itself on proprietary microsphere manufacturing, abuse-deterrent formulations, low reported abuse rates, and dedicated sales forces, though it acknowledges being a smaller company with fewer resources than major competitors.

The company faces material regulatory and legal headwinds. In September 2025, the FDA issued untitled and warning letters citing allegedly misleading claims in direct-to-consumer advertising of prescription products, reflecting increased regulatory scrutiny of promotional practices. In July 2025, the FDA announced mandatory safety-related labeling changes for all opioid pain medications requiring clearer risk information, enhanced warnings, dosing limits, and safe discontinuation instructions. The same month, the FDA required revised labeling for all extended-release ADHD products to warn of weight loss and adverse reactions in children under six. Additionally, the FDA modified the opioid REMS program in October 2024 to require pre-paid drug mail-back envelopes by March 31, 2025. The company is defending four pending litigation matters: a patent challenge from Purdue Pharma over Xtampza ER, Paragraph IV certifications against Belbuca from generic competitors, and investigations from four state attorneys general regarding opioid sales and marketing. Collegium previously settled 27 opioid-related lawsuits in March 2022 for $2.75 million and an Assurance of Discontinuance with Massachusetts in December 2021.

Collegium's operations depend heavily on concentrated supplier relationships and third-party manufacturers across multiple U.S. locations. Active pharmaceutical ingredients are sourced from sole or limited suppliers, creating supply vulnerability. Critical manufacturing is contracted to Patheon (a Thermo Fisher Scientific subsidiary) for Xtampza ER and Nucynta ER, with Jornay PM drug product manufactured by Coating Place in Wisconsin and capsule operations transitioning to Patheon in Cincinnati starting 2026. Belbuca laminate production is split between Adhesives Research in Pennsylvania and LTS Therapy Systems in Minnesota. Nucynta IR is made by Halo Pharmaceutical in New Jersey, and Symproic is produced by UPM Pharmaceuticals in Tennessee with packaging by Sharp Packaging Solutions in Pennsylvania. The company disclosed reliance on third-party manufacturers and DEA quota limitations for controlled substances as structural disadvantages, alongside exposure to patent expirations and generic competition, mandatory REMS program costs, and pricing and reimbursement pressures.

The company acquired Ironshore Therapeutics in 2024 to support Jornay PM commercialization and is expanding its ADHD sales force to approximately 200 representatives. Manufacturing transitions are underway, including relocation of Jornay PM bottling and packing from Puerto Rico to Ohio beginning 2026. Nucynta generics are expected to launch in Q1 2026, though pediatric exclusivity extends through 2027. In December 2025, Collegium secured a new $580 million term loan and $100 million revolving

### PRGS
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/876167/000087616726000008/prgs-20251130.htm)_
