### AAT
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1500217/000150021726000008/aat-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: none._

American Assets Trust, Inc. is a self-administered real estate investment trust operating a diversified portfolio of income-producing properties across the West Coast and Hawaii. The company manages four operating segments: office properties comprising twelve assets with 4.3 million rentable square feet; retail shopping centers with eleven properties totaling 2.4 million rentable square feet; multifamily apartments across seven properties plus one RV resort containing 2,302 units including 120 RV spaces; and a mixed-use property consisting of a 369-room all-suite hotel and approximately 94,000 rentable square feet of retail space. The portfolio is concentrated in primary markets across Southern California, Northern California, Washington, Oregon, and Hawaii, with secondary exposure to Texas. Revenue declined 4.7% to $436.2 million in the most recent period from $457.9 million in the prior year, though net income reached $71.4 million. The company positions itself on irreplaceable in-fill locations with scarce developable land in high-barrier-to-entry markets, backed by experienced senior management, vertically integrated operations, and development and redevelopment expertise.

American Assets Trust completed meaningful capital activity during the recent period. The company sold assets for $117.8 million in 2025 and acquired properties for $67.9 million, including the February 28, 2025 acquisition of Genesee Park and the February 25, 2025 sale of Del Monte Center. Development progress continued with La Jolla Commons III placed in service on April 1, 2025, and One Beach Street fully operational as of August 1, 2024 following renovations. The Lloyd Portfolio is positioned for future phase development.

The company faces significant structural constraints that shape its operating environment. Office segment revenues carry material tenant concentration, with LPL Holdings, Inc. at La Jolla Commons accounting for approximately 13.1% of office revenues and Google LLC at The Landmark at One Market representing 13.3% of office revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025. Retail properties depend on anchor tenants and are exposed to co-tenancy and go-dark provisions in lease agreements. The portfolio exhibits pronounced geographic concentration in California, Washington, Oregon, Texas, and Hawaii, creating exposure to earthquakes, wildfires, tropical storms, and other natural disasters. The company competes against investors with substantially greater financial resources, discount retailers, internet retailers, and other multifamily operators, while confronting secular headwinds from work-from-home trends reducing office demand and competition from owner-occupied housing alternatives. Substantial indebtedness exposes the company to default risk, and the illiquidity of real estate investments limits its ability to respond rapidly to adverse changes.

Ernst & Young LLP serves as auditor. Disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting are effective. No revenue or earnings guidance was provided.

### CCS
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1576940/000157694026000005/ccs-20251231x10k.htm)_

_Triggers: none._

Century Communities, Inc. is a homebuilder operating across 16 states with integrated financial services and a nascent multi-family rental platform. The company operates through five homebuilding segments—West (California, Washington), Mountain (Arizona, Colorado, Nevada, Utah), Texas, Southeast (Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee), and Century Complete (nine states across the South and Midwest)—alongside Financial Services, which provides mortgage origination, title, insurance, and escrow services through four wholly-owned subsidiaries, and Century Living, a Colorado-based multi-family rental development and management operation. Revenue declined 6.4% to $4.1 billion in fiscal 2025 from $4.4 billion in fiscal 2024, while gross margin compressed to 17.6%. The company positions itself through affordability-focused offerings, move-in-ready inventory to accelerate construction cycles, centralized digital marketing capability, and dual brands serving distinct buyer tiers.

Century Communities recorded inventory impairment charges of $21.8 million in fiscal 2025 across 11 communities, with $19.6 million tied to actively selling communities and $2.2 million for finished lots in the Century Complete segment. This follows $8.8 million in impairment charges across 9 communities in fiscal 2024, suggesting ongoing pressure in select markets or community-specific underperformance. The company completed acquisitions of Anglia Homes LP and Landmark Homes of Tennessee, Inc. during 2024, expanding its footprint in existing geographies.

The company's structural position reflects inherent scale disadvantages. Century Communities acknowledges being smaller than many competitors with less geographic diversification despite operating in 16 states, and facing competitors with longer operating histories, greater resources, and lower costs of capital. Established competitors maintain deeper subcontractor and supplier relationships, while Century Communities operates with limited long-term subcontractor contracts, creating exposure to labor constraints. The concentration of operations in 16 states amplifies localized economic risk. The multi-family rental segment remains nascent relative to entrenched REITs, and Century Living depends on eventual asset disposition post-lease stabilization. The Financial Services segment relies on the secondary mortgage market to sell originated loans, creating execution risk beyond direct origination control.

Century Communities is pursuing increased emphasis on affordable housing across all segments, implementing strategic lot pipeline management through option contract utilization, expanding digital marketing and website purchase capability, executing a post-stabilization disposition strategy for Century Living assets, and optimizing supply chain operations in response to tariff impacts on building materials. No revenue or earnings guidance was provided.

### WABC
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/311094/000117184326001195/wabc20251231_10k.htm)_

_Triggers: none._

Westamerica Bancorporation operates a single banking segment through subsidiary Westamerica Bank, providing a full range of banking services to individual and commercial customers across Northern and Central California. The company's product suite spans commercial loans, commercial real estate loans, construction lending, residential real estate loans, consumer installment loans, deposit accounts, investment securities, trust services, merchant processing, and debit card services. Revenue declined 12.2% to $258.1 million in the filing period from $293.8 million in the prior year, with net income of $116.2 million. The company positions itself around strategic focus on banking needs of small businesses and regional concentration in its California markets, supported by an experienced senior management team and well-capitalized regulatory status.

The competitive environment presents structural headwinds. Westamerica faces competition from major banks, smaller community banks, savings and loan associations, credit unions, thrift institutions, mortgage brokerages, insurance companies, internet-based fintech providers, brokerage houses, mutual fund companies, credit card companies, non-bank lenders, asset-based lenders, government-sponsored lenders, securities brokerages, consumer finance companies, and money market mutual funds. Many competitors possess substantially greater financial and technological resources, offer lower interest rates and more liberal loan terms, and in the case of non-bank fintech providers, operate with fewer regulatory constraints. This fragmented competitive landscape combined with intense competition for deposits and loans constrains pricing power.

Westamerica's structural position carries concentrated risks. Geographic concentration in California exposes the company to state-specific economic downturns. The loan portfolio's dependence on real estate makes it vulnerable to property value declines. Extensive federal and state banking regulation imposes substantial compliance costs that smaller competitors may avoid or manage differently. The company operates without identified material concentrations in any single customer or vendor, but the nature of regional retail and commercial banking inherently limits scale advantages relative to national competitors. Disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting are both effective, and no material weaknesses have been disclosed.

The company has not provided revenue or earnings guidance. No material litigation, regulatory actions, acquisitions, impairments, or significant facility events are disclosed in the extraction.

### FBRT
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1562528/000156252826000008/bsprt-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: none._

Franklin BSP Realty Trust, Inc. operates two complementary segments in commercial real estate finance. The Commercial Real Estate Financing segment originates, acquires, and asset manages commercial real estate debt across a spectrum of instruments including first mortgage loans, subordinated mortgage loans, mezzanine loans, and participations, alongside real estate securities such as CMBS and CDO notes. The Agency Business segment originates and sells multifamily finance products under programs sponsored by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, Ginnie Mae, and HUD, while retaining servicing and asset management responsibilities on substantially all loans it originates and sells. Revenue declined 18.2% to $430.3 million in the filing period from $526.1 million in the prior year, though net income reached $84.1 million. The company positions itself through conservative underwriting, comprehensive due diligence, direct origination relationships, and access to government-sponsored enterprise programs through its advisor's established credit platform.

The company completed its acquisition of NewPoint Holdings JV LLC for $297.3 million effective July 1, 2025, substantially expanding its Agency Business capacity. This transaction enables Franklin BSP to originate multifamily finance products across Fannie Mae's DUS program, Freddie Mac's Program Plus offering, and HUD's MAP and Section 232 LEAN programs, along with Ginnie Mae issuance capabilities. During the period, the company also executed CLO 2025-FL12 with $1.1 billion in issuance and continued conduit loan origination for CMBS securitization sales.

The company operates at a structural disadvantage relative to many peers. It explicitly acknowledges it has less financial resources and a higher cost of capital than many competitors, faces REIT operating constraints that others do not, and is subject to Investment Company Act registration requirements. Competitors span a broad category including other mortgage REITs, specialty finance companies, banks, mortgage bankers, insurance companies, mutual funds, hedge funds, and institutional investors. Many of these competitors operate with greater resources, lower cost of capital, and higher risk tolerances. Franklin BSP's stated advantages—conservative underwriting, comprehensive due diligence, direct origination relationships, and structuring capability—are positioned as compensating factors, though the revenue decline during the period suggests headwinds in the current operating environment.

The company disclosed related party transactions and maintains effective disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting, with PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP serving as auditor. No guidance on future revenue or earnings was provided.

### WOR
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/108516/000095017025100137/wor-20250531.htm)_

_Triggers: none._

Worthington Enterprises manufactures and distributes consumer products and building solutions across two primary segments. The Consumer Products segment markets tools, outdoor living, and celebrations products under established brands including Balloon Time, Bernzomatic, Coleman (licensed), and Level5, selling primarily through mass merchandisers and retailers. The Building Products segment supplies pressurized containment solutions for heating, cooling, and water applications—refrigerant cylinders, LPG tanks, and expansion tanks—alongside ceiling suspension systems and light gauge metal framing through unconsolidated joint ventures WAVE and ClarkDietrich. The company operates primarily in the United States with secondary exposure to Europe, Canada, and international markets. Revenue declined 7.4% to $1.15 billion in fiscal 2025 from $1.25 billion in the prior year, with gross margin at 27.6% and operating margin at negative 0.9%, reflecting compressed profitability across the business.

The company recorded a $50.1 million impairment of GTI indefinite-lived intangible assets in fiscal 2025, signaling asset write-downs tied to underperformance. During the period covered by this filing, Worthington completed three acquisitions: Ragasco for $108.6 million in 2024 (composite propane cylinder production), Halo for $9.6 million in 2024, and Elgen for $93 million in 2025 (HVAC components and ductwork expansion). The company also established a joint venture with Hexagon in 2024 to pursue Sustainable Energy Solutions hydrogen infrastructure opportunities. These transactions reflect management's strategy to expand into adjacent product categories and emerging energy applications, though the timing coincides with revenue contraction and operating margin deterioration that warrant scrutiny of integration execution and capital efficiency.

Customer concentration presents a structural risk. One retail customer represented 12% of consolidated net sales in fiscal 2025, while the Consumer Products segment's largest customer accounted for approximately 28% of segment revenue. In the low-pressure LPG cylinder market, Worthington holds the largest domestic market share but faces one principal domestic competitor alongside multiple regional and foreign competitors. Price competition, customer consolidation in retail, and cyclicality in consumer products and construction end markets constrain margins. The company sources steel through a supply agreement with Worthington Steel (divested in 2023), aluminum subject to Section 232 tariffs, and propane, propylene, and helium with portions secured under fixed-price agreements, creating exposure to commodity sourcing dynamics and tariff variability.

Management's forward initiatives center on integrating recent acquisitions—Elgen's HVAC footprint, Ragasco's composite cylinder production, and ClarkDietrich light gauge steel expansion—while scaling the Worthington Business System continuous improvement program across facilities. The company discloses use of adjusted operating income, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EPS, and adjusted effective tax rate as non-GAAP measures. No revenue or earnings guidance is provided. The impairment charge, margin compression, and acquisition integration agenda suggest near-term earnings headwinds despite strategic repositioning in building products and emerging energy applications.

### ICHR
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652535/000165253526000012/ichr-20251226.htm)_

_Triggers: none._

Ichor Holdings designs, engineers, and manufactures critical fluid delivery subsystems and components for semiconductor capital equipment. The company's primary segment encompasses gas delivery subsystems, chemical delivery products, weldments, valves, advanced flow control systems, and precision machining. Revenue grew 11.6% to $947.7 million in fiscal 2025, though profitability deteriorated significantly with gross margin of 9.3% and an operating margin of negative 4.1%, resulting in a net loss of $52.8 million. The company operates manufacturing facilities across the United States, Singapore, Malaysia, and Mexico, positioning itself near major customer locations. Ichor competes on deep fluids engineering expertise, long-standing OEM relationships, operational experience spanning 20+ years, and proprietary advanced flow control technology, distinguishing itself against Ultra Clean Technology and numerous smaller competitors as well as internal manufacturing groups within OEM organizations.

The company initiated a geographic footprint rationalization and restructuring plan in fiscal 2025, closing its Scotland and Korea operations and consolidating manufacturing activities to high-volume facilities. This restructuring generated substantial charges: $19.8 million in inventory impairments, $3.1 million in fixed asset impairments, $900,000 in operating lease right-of-use asset impairments from the consolidation plan, plus an additional $1.3 million in lease impairments and $1.7 million in inventory write-offs tied to the Scotland and Korea exits. Combined, these impairment and write-off charges totaled approximately $26.8 million in fiscal 2025, explaining the gap between modest revenue growth and sharp operating loss.

The business model carries acute concentration risk. Lam Research and Applied Materials together accounted for 76% of total sales in 2025, each individually exceeding 10% of revenues. This customer concentration, combined with limited backlog and short order timeframes, constrains sales forecasting reliability. The company explicitly acknowledges dependence on a small number of OEM customers, customer pricing leverage, vulnerability to sole-sourcing decisions, and exposure to the cyclically volatile semiconductor industry. Manufacturing complexity and reliance on trade secrets rather than patents for intellectual property protection present additional structural vulnerabilities. Competitors with greater financial and technical resources pose ongoing competitive pressure.

Ichor is executing manufacturing consolidation to high-volume facilities and expanding its product portfolio to include proprietary components as part of the 2025 restructuring initiative. The company has not provided revenue or earnings guidance for future periods.
